response.sql: SELECT invoice_number, COUNT(*) AS transaction_count FROM Financial_Transactions WHERE invoice_number IS NOT NULL GROUP BY invoice_number HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN transaction_type = 'Payment' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 ORDER BY transaction_count DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: 'Exactly Payment' is read as a case-sensitive match on transaction_type = 'Payment'. In SQLite and some other databases '=' is case-sensitive, but in MySQL with a default collation it is not, so the comparison could also match values like 'payment'.
Ties in transaction count are broken arbitrarily, so the top 10 may vary if several invoices share the 10th-highest count.
